title: Sorry, I Wasn't Listening: The Halftime Speech
trend: Instagram Reels 'Sorry, I Wasn't Listening' (text admits daydreaming about something specific; New Engen Instagram list updated Nov 6 2026, US) + basketball season tipping off (college basketball among top US Google searches, Nov 9 2026) — a youth basketball coach gives a fiery halftime speech while her players and the basketball admit they were daydreaming; twist: the team is actually up by twenty (she read the wrong side of the scoreboard) and she was daydreaming about the nacho cheese pump too
youtube_title: Sorry, I wasn't listening: the halftime speech 🏀
description:
Coach Rhonda has a big halftime speech ready. Jalen is thinking about nachos, Mia is watching a dog in a hat, and the basketball has feelings for the floor.

lines.text: Halftime. Bring it in. We are down by twenty and I have a speech.
Coach, I am so sorry. I was not listening. I was thinking about nachos.
I have not started the speech yet, Jalen.
I know. I was getting ahead.
Okay. Listen. Defense is a feeling. You feel the other guy.
You feel his breathing. You become his shadow. Did you hear me?
Sorry. I wasn't listening. The nacho cheese has a pump.
A pump.
You push it and the cheese just comes out. Like a little cheese volcano.
Jalen, there is a game.
There is also a volcano.
Mia. You are my point guard. You are my brain. Talk to me.
Sorry, Coach. I wasn't listening. There is a dog in row three in a little hat.
We do not look at the crowd.
He is wearing a hat and a tiny jersey. He has better posture than me.
He clapped earlier.
He did not clap. He wagged. It counts.
When I was your age I did not see dogs. I saw the basket.
Did the basket have a hat?
No.
Fine. Ball. You were out there all half. What did you see?
Sorry, I wasn't listening. I was thinking about the floor.
The floor.
I hit the floor four hundred times a game. At some point it becomes a relationship.
Is it serious?
She squeaks when I land. That is how I know she cares.
That is the sneakers.
Do not take this from me.
Everybody. Eyes on me. This is the part where I get loud.
We pass! We move! We box out! We want it more than them!
Did anybody hear any of that?
I heard want.
I heard box. I thought of the dog in a box.
I heard out. I would love to go out. With the floor.
You are ten years old and a ball. How are we this bad at listening?
Coach, can I ask a question?
Is it about defense?
It is about the score.
We are down twenty. I looked at it at the buzzer.
Coach, we are home. Home is on the left.
I know where home is.
You were reading the right. That is the other team.
Say that again. Slowly.
We are up by twenty.
I knew that. I was there for every point. I just was not listening.
So the speech was for the other team?
The speech was for everyone. It was a general speech.
Coach. Were you listening to the game?
Sorry. I wasn't listening.
I was thinking about the nachos.
The pump?
The pump. I pushed it at the start of the half. I have been thinking about it since.
That is why you kept looking at the snack stand.
I was looking at the defense near the snack stand.
Nobody plays defense near the snack stand. I have seen it.
Okay. New plan. Same as the old plan, but we are winning.
And after the game?
Nachos for everyone. Even the ball.
Can the floor come?
The floor stays. The floor has a job.
Can the dog in the hat come?
Yes. He has better posture than all of us.
Coach, what was the speech about again?
Sorry. I wasn't listening.
